PullRequest.Title: Artifact integrations: keep references in the References pill and present item actions on their item
PullRequest.Body:

Two fixes to how integrated artifacts show up in the Agents window.

### References stay in the References pill

Before this change, a reference whose integration set a `groupId` got a pill of its own, and references never joined a group. Two things looked wrong as a result:

- Three ExP scorecard links recorded as references collapsed into one stray `ExP 13d3ffbb` pill next to the `4 Experiments` group.
- A commit recorded as a reference was the only entry in the References pill, so it showed inline like a pill of its own.

Now only **artifacts** get a pill of their own from a `groupId`. References are always listed in the References pill with the other references. If a reference points at the same resource as an artifact that has a pill of its own, it's hidden and represented by that artifact, the same way alias collapsing already works.

- `SessionArtifacts.hasOwnPill` is true only for artifacts in the focused chat.
- Alias collapsing now also covers records with a group ID, so a reference is hidden when an artifact with its own pill stands in for it.
- The `groupId` docs in the proposed API and in `ARTIFACT_INTEGRATIONS_PROPOSAL.md` now say this.

### Item actions show only their item

When **Fix Issue** ran on one row of a test plan item's **Reported Issues** list, the prompt it sent was right, but the chat request showed it as **Fix Issues…** with every reported issue listed. It looked like the agent was fixing all of them.

When a registered action runs for one details item (input `{ detailsId, itemId }`), `ArtifactExecutionService` now presents the request as the item action (**Fix Issue**, with its icon), and its details contain only that item.

### Validation

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/common/artifactIntegrations.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sessionArtifacts.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/artifactIntegrationGroup.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/artifactIntegrationPresentation.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatArtifactActionContentPart.test.ts` | Passed: 332 tests |
| The two new tests, without the source changes | Failed: 2 tests |
| `pnpm run typecheck-client` | Passed |
| `pnpm run eslint <changed files>` | Passed |

I also checked it end to end in a Code OSS build of this branch, using the Team Tools extension from microsoft/vscode-packages#437, with real ExP, GitHub and test plan item data. I drove the Agents window with dbgjs:

- Recording the same artifacts and references as the reported session now shows `2 Issues`, `4 Experiments`, `Program.cs` and `2 References` (the commit and the scorecards). Before, it showed separate `ExP 13d3ffbb` and `Commit 432b367` pills.
- With the commit recorded as an artifact, it's listed in the Artifacts dropdown with the other artifacts.
- **Fix Issue** on one reported issue of a real test plan item is now shown as **Fix Issue: TPI #346602** with only that issue under **Reported Issues**.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The retention path and absence of eviction are explicit in the changed code, and model/resource ownership confirms that UI model disposal no longer releases the latest graph. Exact heap impact depends on extension list sizes and how many artifact details users browse, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained ArtifactDetails object graphs, including item arrays and their strings/resources
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained memory grows with the total size of every details section acquired across all live artifact resources; partial/load-more lists increase each retained graph, and changing presentation details IDs can grow the map because removed IDs are never evicted.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased retained heap and subsequent GC pressure while browsing artifact details in a long-lived session
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The bridge retained the resource's original initialDetails snapshot, but a later details snapshot was owned by the active ExtensionArtifactDetails model and became collectible when that model was disposed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every result or update received by a details model is now stored in latestDetails, while initialDetails remains retained too; disposing the model does not remove either cache entry, and acceptState does not prune IDs that are no longer exposed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added callback at line 338 stores each full details snapshot in latestDetails; the same diff adds latestDetails as a resource-lifetime Map and leaves the existing initialDetails record intact.
Findings.Title: Reuse or evict cached detail snapshots after model disposal
Findings.Impact: After a user opens or pages details for many artifacts, those full snapshots remain reachable even after each details view closes; long-lived sessions therefore accumulate duplicate list data and consume more memory until the artifact resource is released.
Findings.Evidence: ExtensionArtifactDetails.accept invokes the new received callback for both the acquire result and every extension update. ExtensionArtifactResource owns latestDetails for its whole lifetime and has no delete/clear path. The existing initialDetails record still holds the original full snapshot. The proposed API supports partial details with loadMore, so these snapshots can contain large item arrays. SessionArtifacts keeps an artifact integration reference for each record in the focused chat, so closing the details UI disposes the model but not the resource or this cache.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a single per-ID snapshot cache seeded from initialDetails and replace its entry on updates (keeping canLoadMore separately), prune IDs when acceptState removes them, and avoid retaining a second full snapshot after the last details model closes unless it is required for a pending item-action presentation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run a registered prompt action from one artifact details item
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authorization and the extension's existing providePrompt call must complete, then presentation capture and chat submission run. The new item lookup reads a cached snapshot synchronously; its follow-up details acquisition RPC is launched but not awaited, so that RPC is off the chat-submission critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare the registered prompt action in the extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extension-host prompt preparation was awaited before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before presentation capture and chat submission

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and immediately dispose the details model used to identify the selected item
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquire/dispose pair for the selected details ID; before the diff captureLinkedDetails acquired each unique linked details part, while actions supplying explicit prompt details previously needed none
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Presentation capture scanned all linked details parts when prompt details were absent, or performed no details acquisition when the action supplied prompt details.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cached value is read synchronously; the acquire promise is not awaited, so extension-host work is off the direct submission critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the prepared prompt to the chat runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same chat submission occurred before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected item and one details ID per action execution; retries can repeat preparation, but normal UI state prevents the same item action from being requested concurrently while its run is unsettled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One run per selected item is admitted by the UI's pending-run guard. The bridge creates one transient details model for capture and immediately disposes it; extension-host transport handles the acquire/dispose messages. There is no collection-wide concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm latestDetails entry supplies the synchronous item snapshot. Cold resources fall back to initialDetails. Even on a warm hit the transient model still initiates an extension-host acquire, but for ordinary item actions this replaces the previous captureLinkedDetails scan rather than adding broad fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the execution path, cache read, immediate disposal, and extension-host messages are explicit. The changed path generally reduces linked-section fan-out to one selected section.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific acquireDetails work varies; the extra call only occurs relative to the old path when promptDetails are explicitly supplied, so this does not independently justify another finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable latency or fan-out regression. The dedicated lookup is bounded to one details ID and usually replaces a wider pre-existing linked-details scan.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, update, page, and close artifact detail lists across a focused session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening details awaits the artifact model's details acquisition and extension-host result. Later updates/loadMore cross the extension-host boundary before rendering. Closing the details UI disposes the model, but the newly added latestDetails cache remains reachable from the live artifact resource.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire details and serialize the complete ArtifactDetails snapshot from the extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition per active details model, coalesced by the platform binding for same-artifact/same-ID consumers
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same acquire and serialization occurred, but returned/updated snapshots became collectible after the details model was disposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial acquire is awaited by the details view; subsequent change notifications update rendering

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load another details page through the extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per user load-more request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Load-more already crossed the same boundary; the changed cache now keeps its resulting snapshot after model disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the requested page is presented

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total detail snapshot size across every details ID acquired for every live artifact record; item arrays can be partial/paged, and state revisions may expose different IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ArtifactBinding coalesces simultaneous consumers of the same details ID behind one provider model. Different artifacts and IDs remain independent. The regression is retained state after consumers reach zero, not concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold creation retains initialDetails for every exposed section. The diff adds a second resource-lifetime latestDetails cache populated by acquire results and updates. Entries are neither removed when the last model closes nor pruned when state stops exposing an ID.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: received snapshots are stored in a Map owned by ExtensionArtifactResource, initialDetails is still retained, and there is no eviction path before resource disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual heap growth depends on extension snapshot sizes, paging representation, records in the focused chat, and browsing behavior; these affect severity but not the retention mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: full updated snapshots survive details-model disposal and duplicate the retained initial snapshot, increasing heap and GC pressure over a long-lived browsing session.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update Artifacts/References pills for the focused chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable recomputation filters the focused chat's records, collapses aliases, and builds pill sections before the toolbar rerenders. Integration acquisition, GitHub resolution, and other resource work were already scheduled by existing SessionArtifacts ownership.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire artifact integration presentations for session records
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one live acquisition per record ID, guarded by lifetimes.has; unchanged by the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-record acquisitions occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Presentations arrive asynchronously and update pills; initial generic pill rendering does not wait for all acquisitions

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub reference and commit metadata through existing resolvers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped/cached by retained resource identities and commit targets; unchanged by the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolver retention and asynchronous lookup behavior existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous metadata enrichment, not newly placed on the synchronous pill-filter path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of records in the focused chat after alias collapsing; hasOwnPill performs cached Set membership and snapshot reads per record.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-record integration acquisitions may run concurrently. The diff adds only an in-memory derived Set and changes candidate filtering; it introduces no limiter change or new boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _artifactIds is a derived Set cached until chatArtifacts changes. Existing presentations and GitHub resolver caches retain their prior ownership and invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk adds cached Set membership and changes which records participate in existing in-memory alias collapse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large chats increase existing O(n) recomputation, but the diff does not change its asymptotic complexity or add expensive boundaries.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The extra derived Set is bounded by focused-chat records and avoids recomputing artifact classification inside each hasOwnPill call.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files. Traced item-action execution, extension-host details acquisition/serialization, details cache ownership, and focused-chat pill rendering. Submitted one cache-lifecycle finding for resource-lifetime retention of full latest detail snapshots; no additional hot-path, fan-out, concurrency, or rendering regression met the evidence threshold.
